page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8175M processor operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 16 vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. CPU cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX and AVX-512, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering a standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no bundled local instance storage, requiring users to attach Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem operations. Baseline network performance is configured at 5 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated by default. The configuration lacks dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results show clear separation between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. Single-core throughput places in the lower quartile of current cloud benchmarks, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1282.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1034.0. In contrast, parallelized performance sits solidly in the middle 50% tier, evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng metric of 13479.83, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6542.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 14441.4. Large block memory read bandwidth achieves 87.77 GB/sec, while write operations peak at 45.25 GB/sec.

Application benchmarks reflect steady throughput for balanced multi-threaded tasks, recording 13.15 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 11.92 GB/sec in static web serving tests. The instance offers reliable, balanced resource distribution at scale, though tasks bound strictly to single-core execution speed or requiring high-speed local NVMe scratch space will face architectural bottlenecks. Best-fit use cases include enterprise application servers, mid-sized relational database hosting on networked storage, CI/CD runners, containerized web clusters, and batch data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based virtual server powered by a dedicated 16-vCPU, 8-core Intel Xeon 8175M x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance is paired with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage, relying instead on network-attached EBS volumes, and provides a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Across synthetic benchmarks, the m5.4xlarge exhibits lower-tier single-core instruction throughput, balanced by middle-tier multi-threaded processing power and standard DDR4 memory bandwidth. Practical throughput reaches 13.15 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.92 GB/sec in static web delivery. This resource allocation makes the m5.4xlarge well suited for horizontally scaled web services, microservice containers, enterprise application servers, and general batch processing workloads requiring dependable multi-core execution.
